title: Play any video stream
intro: Paste a link to a live or on-demand stream. HLS, DASH, MP4, WebM, FLV and MPEG-TS all play right here in your browser.

formats.name: Audio (MP3, AAC, M4A, Opus, WAV, FLAC)

guide: This player plays video streams straight from a link. It runs entirely in your browser: the video travels directly from the stream’s server to your screen, and nothing passes through us.
Paste the address of a stream into the box above and press Play. You can also open the player directly by adding the stream address to the page URL:
If the stream address contains its own `?` or `&`, put `url=` last or encode the address first. The box above does this for you.

The player reads the end of the link (`.m3u8`, `.mpd`, `.mp4` and so on) and loads the right playback engine. If the link has no recognisable ending, it tries the browser’s built-in player, then HLS, then DASH, until one works. To force a specific engine, add `type=` before the link, for example `/player?type=hls&url=…` (also `dash`, `flv`, `ts` or `native`).
Live streams get a Live badge and a button that jumps back to the live edge; if the stream keeps a rewind window, you can scrub back through it. The settings menu (the gear) lets you choose:

list.title: Quality
list.text: Pick a resolution, or leave it on Auto to follow your connection. Auto shows which quality is playing right now.

list.title: Audio and subtitles
list.text: Switch language or surround track when the stream offers more than one. The `CC` button turns subtitles on and off.

list.title: Stats for nerds
list.text: Engine, resolution, bitrate, connection speed, buffer, dropped frames and live latency, updated every second.

list.title: Copy link at current time
list.text: Shares the stream starting where you are, using `t=` in the address.

guide: On-demand videos remember where you stopped and offer to resume next time. On phones, double-tap the left or right side of the video to skip 10 seconds.

Instead of a bare stream address, a link can point at a JSON endpoint that describes the video. The player fetches it and builds the whole page from it: title, description, poster, chapters, subtitles, a countdown for scheduled streams and an Up next list.
The endpoint returns JSON like this. Only `source` is required; everything else is optional.

guide.code:
{
  "title": "Big Buck Bunny",
  "description": "Plain text. Blank lines start new paragraphs; links are clickable.",
  "channel": "Open Movie Night",
  "publishedAt": "2026-11-08T18:00:00Z",
  "startsAt": "2026-12-31T23:00:00Z",
  "poster": "https://example.com/poster.jpg",
  "tags": ["Animation", "Short film"],
  "source": { "url": "https://example.com/video/master.m3u8", "type": "hls" },
  "subtitles": [{ "label": "English", "lang": "en", "url": "subs/en.vtt", "default": false }],
  "chapters": [{ "time": 0, "title": "Opening" }, { "time": 150, "title": "Trouble arrives" }],
  "related": [
    { "endpoint": "next-video.json", "title": "Next video", "poster": "…", "duration": "4:12" },
    { "url": "https://example.com/clip.mp4", "title": "A plain clip", "live": false }
  ]
}

list.title: source or sources
list.text: One stream, or a list to try in order (for example HLS first, MP4 as a fallback). `type` can be `hls`, `dash`, `flv`, `ts` or `native`.

list.title: Relative links
list.text: Links inside the JSON, such as subtitle files or related endpoints, are resolved against the endpoint’s own address.

list.title: startsAt
list.text: If the time is in the future, the page shows a countdown and starts the stream automatically.

list.title: subtitles
list.text: WebVTT or SRT files. They appear in the subtitles menu alongside any tracks built into the stream.

list.title: related
list.text: Each item links to another `endpoint` (opens as a rich link) or a plain `url`. The first one plays automatically when a video ends.

list.title: Hosting
list.text: Endpoints on another site must allow cross-origin requests (CORS). Files in this site’s `data/streams/` folder work as-is. `type=fetch&url=…` is accepted as an alias for `endpoint=`.

list.title: The server blocks other websites
list.text: Many streams only allow playback on their own site, using a browser rule called CORS. Nothing on this page can override that.

list.title: The link has expired
list.text: Signed links from many providers stop working after a few minutes or hours. Copy a fresh one.

list.title: It is protected by DRM
list.text: Encrypted streams from subscription services need licences this player doesn’t have.

list.title: The protocol isn’t made for browsers
list.text: RTMP, RTSP and UDP streams can’t play in any web browser. Ask the provider for an HLS or DASH address instead.

list.title: Secure page, insecure stream
list.text: When this page is served over HTTPS, browsers block streams on plain `http://` addresses.

list.title: The codec isn’t supported
list.text: Some files, such as AVI, WMV or H.265 video on older systems, can’t be decoded by every browser.

playNote: The stream plays directly from its source to your browser; nothing passes through our servers. To watch something else, choose New stream, or change the address after `/player?url=` or `/player?endpoint=`.
